summary: Field-sieve: timeboxed request for minimized prod payload review to validate billing anomaly
description: Issue summary: Finance and Support flagged a customer billing spike that appears correlated with a recent model rollout. To investigate, Support requests one-time access to a tightly scoped, field-level redacted sample of production inference payloads (request+response metadata) for the affected tenant. Impact: inability to confirm whether the spike is caused by legitimate traffic, a caching regression, or repeated retries; billing dispute escalated by customer. Environment: production, us-east. Scope requested: 2-hour window (2026-02-25 14:00-16:00 UTC), up to 500 request records, field-level redaction applied to PII-sensitive fields (user_message, user_id replaced with stable hashes, embeddings and raw token text replaced with token-length metadata and first-3-chars masked), include routing metadata (model_version, route, response_latency_ms, retry_count) and cost metrics (tokens_in/tokens_out). Justification: minimal sample required for triage and to prepare a customer-facing billing explanation. Proposed guardrails: export written to restricted S3 bucket (s3://redwood-internal/samples/INT-130821/), encryption with KMS key rw-prod-log-read, read-only IAM role time-limited (4 hours), full access audit trail, and DO NOT re-run or replay payloads. Requester is Support (Priya Shah) plus Finance (Miguel Torres) read-only. Approval checklist below must be completed before access is granted.
comments: 2026-03-01 09:12 - Priya Shah: Filing request after customer (Acme Analytics) disputed Feb 25 invoice. Finance sees +420% token usage on their project id; top-line appears to align with new rw-instruct-1 rollout. Need minimally exposed samples to verify whether traffic is legitimate.

2026-03-01 10:03 - Miguel Torres (Finance): Confirmed enlarged token counts. Prefers redacted samples to avoid sharing PII with Finance team. Will coordinate wording for customer communication once we have root cause.

2026-03-02 15:44 - Security (Aisha Khan): Redaction requirements noted. We require stable hashing for user identifiers and masking for free-text fields. No raw customer content to leave Redwood boundary. Also need justification and explicit list of viewers. Will not approve until S3 path and IAM ephemeral role defined.

2026-03-03 08:20 - Liam O'Connor (Assignee): Drafted minimal extraction job spec and retasked an infra ticket to create time-limited role. Asking SRE to confirm export performance does not affect serving runtime.

2026-03-04 11:50 - SRE (Jordan Lee): Confirmed extract can be run from offline telemetry index. No impact on serving runtime. Recommended export via streaming consumer into a processing Lambda that applies redaction in flight and writes to locked S3 prefix.

2026-03-05 16:30 - Security (Aisha Khan): Conditional approval granted with the following conditions met: KMS key policy in place, IAM role bound to rw-observed-sessions-read-only for the specific S3 prefix, and audit logging enabled to push to secure Splunk index. Please attach final export manifest here after run.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: rollout changed batching/prefix caching behavior causing duplicate work and inflated token counting on certain routes. Hypothesis B: customer integration is retrying failed streaming sessions post-rollout. Data needed: pairing of routing metadata with token counts and retry_count per session. We validated that rw-instruct-1 was promoted to default routing for the customer on 2026-02-24 23:48 UTC. Initial query of aggregated telemetry shows increased mean tokens per session from 120 -> 730 for that customer's project id starting 2026-02-25 14:00 UTC. Need raw-ish records to attribute upstream cause and confirm whether internal retries or client retries are root cause.
resolution: Pending run. Planned resolution path: - Run timeboxed extract with field-sieve redaction. - Security to verify S3/KMS/role before release. - Support and Finance review sample and conclude whether overage is billable. - If internal bug found, create engineering issue and credit customer for incorrect charges. If customer integration is at fault, prepare customer-facing remediation recommendations and invoice adjustment. Post-run, attach export manifest and short findings summary. If access is granted and run completes, update status to In Progress and set final resolution details here.
